title: A list of bytes crosses the guest boundary as one wasmtime `Val` per byte.
text: `convert` lowers `Value::Bytes` to a `Val::List` of `Val::U8` and lifts it back the same way, because the call bridge calls every export through wasmtime's dynamic `Func::call_async`. Each byte costs a whole `Val` on the host, so a crossing costs tens of nanoseconds per byte; `benches/results/image-guest.json` shows returning decoded pixels costing about ten times the decode. Both directions are charged to the request: the hostcall fuel bounds a lift, the lifted results are charged while they are converted, and the lowered arguments are charged until the guest returns (`crates/nvs-ext/src/call.rs`'s `Request::run`). The decided fix is wasmtime's typed calls for exports whose parameters or results are `list<u8>`. A typed call needs a Rust type for every parameter and result, and wasmtime fixes each type's layout at compile time (`ComponentType::ABI`, a `const`), so a type built from the manifest at run time cannot be one. The exports that move the most bytes, such as `image`'s `run(source, plan)`, carry their bytes inside records and variants. The user decided how they are covered: Rust bindings generated for each first-party world (`wit/image.wit`, `wit/pdf.wit`, `wit/intl.wit`, `wit/spreadsheet.wit`), with a conversion from `Value` per world, so every first-party export, `run`, `variants` and `merge` included, makes one copy each way. The WIT does not change, and a third-party export stays on the dynamic path. A typed path for flat signatures only was declined because it leaves `run` per byte, and flattening the worlds because it shapes the API to suit the bridge. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/support/image_arms.rs` sizes its frame for the per-byte cost until then.
